definition: Published monthly level from analytics.fact_housing_observation with row-level lineage in observations.csv. Preserve source missingness and provider imputation flags.
100 times the difference in consecutive natural-log levels within one geography. Positive levels and adjacent calendar months required.
Target is the observed level at the target month. ZHVI is USD; ZORI is USD/month; permits are authorized housing units per month; inventory is a stock counted in homes.
Target is the arithmetic mean of the current and prior two monthly permit flows. Requires all three observed months.
Observed target at the forecast origin (trailing mean for mean3).

Fit current monthly log growth to an intercept and the previous 1/3/6 growth rates by OLS. Retain six warm-up growth months for aligned fits. Iterate predicted growth; origin level times exp(sum of predicted log growth / 100).
Fit target level to an intercept and its previous 1/3 levels by OLS. Allow three warm-up months across these fits. Recursively use forecasts for unobserved lags.

Driftless ARIMA(0,1,1) in log ZHVI. Estimate an invertible MA coefficient on percent log changes by conditional sum of squares with zero presample innovation. First forecast change equals theta times the last innovation; subsequent changes are zero. Exponentiate from the origin without bias correction.
Repeat the most recent observed level or trailing permit mean at every horizon.
Repeat the observed level or mean for the target calendar month one year earlier. At 12 months this equals the no-change forecast.
Fit AR(1) to trailing three-month permit means with an intercept. Iterate directly on this mean.
Fit AR(1) to raw permits after three warm-up months. Compute each predicted trailing mean from its three component months using known months through the origin and recursive forecasts thereafter.

Name of fitted outcome; ordered lag terms; coefficient mapping for the intercept and each RHS term where estimated. Growth slopes operate on percentage-point log changes. Benchmarks estimate no parameters.
Configured first raw observation and actual first/last fitted response months. Lags and differences are built within the configured raw window.
Number of fitted responses in this regression at this origin. Benchmarks have zero fitted responses.
Square root of mean squared one-step training residuals on the fitted response scale. For ARIMA this is the root mean squared conditional innovation.
OLS one minus residual sum of squares / centered response sum of squares. Blank for undefined values and models without a comparable OLS statistic.
The forecast starts at the end of the origin month. The target is exactly h calendar months later.
Forecast at the origin and observed target at the target date. Revised provider series are treated retrospectively.
Forecast minus actual. Positive means the model forecast above the observed target.
Mean absolute forecast error for one series/target/model/window/horizon/split on matched dates.
Square root of mean squared forecast error for the same matched group.

Report comparison calculated as 100 times (1 minus model RMSE divided by reference RMSE) on identical target dates and target definitions. The reference is stated in each table, usually no change; negative means larger error. Undefined when reference RMSE is zero. This is not a share of explained future behavior.
100 times the mean of |forecast minus actual| / |actual| over matched dates. Blank if any actual is zero.
Number of monthly origins scored within the split for one specification and horizon.
Choose the lowest validation RMSE for each geography/variable/target/horizon. Break exact ties by model ID then training start. Join that frozen choice to held-out scores.
Descriptive sample standard deviation of each county's monthly ZHVI log changes over matching six-month test target dates.

100 times one minus the residual variance divided by the total variance of monthly log growth. Residuals subtract each calendar month's mean on matched LA inventory and price dates from the main training start through the first test origin.
